categories.main_business_segments: Kurimoto, Ltd. operates three main business segments: Lifeline Business (manufacturing and sales of ductile iron pipes, valves, and related systems for water and gas infrastructure), Machinery Systems Business (industrial machinery, plant engineering, and cast/forged products), and Industrial & Construction Materials Business (construction materials, lightweight steel pipes, FRP/composite products, and synthetic resin products).
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: The company leverages advanced manufacturing technologies such as ductile iron pipe production, continuous FRP molding, precision casting, and specialized machinery design. It emphasizes proprietary processes for earthquake-resistant water pipes, energy-efficient production, and recycling systems, as well as R&D in composite materials, lead-free copper alloys, and magnesium alloys.
categories.primary_customers_markets: Key customers include public utilities (waterworks, sewage, and gas), construction and civil engineering firms, industrial manufacturers (notably in automotive and energy), and infrastructure maintenance companies. The company serves both public sector (infrastructure renewal, disaster prevention) and private sector (industrial equipment, building materials) markets.
categories.geographic_coverage: Kurimoto's primary operations and sales are concentrated in Japan, which accounts for over 90% of sales and assets. The company also has a presence in North America through subsidiaries, and exports products and systems to overseas markets, particularly in Asia and the US.
categories.supply_chain_position: Kurimoto operates mainly as a midstream and downstream supplier, manufacturing finished products and systems for direct sale to end users, contractors, and public entities, while also providing engineering, installation, and maintenance services.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: Strategic priorities include strengthening stable revenue businesses, investing in growth-driving segments (such as infrastructure maintenance and recycling), and advancing sustainability through decarbonization, circular economy initiatives, and digital transformation (DX). R&D focuses on earthquake-resistant infrastructure, low-carbon materials, recycling technologies, and next-generation battery and composite systems.
categories.revenue_model: The company generates revenue primarily through the sale of manufactured products (pipes, machinery, materials), engineering and construction contracts, and related services. Some revenue is also derived from maintenance, installation, and licensing of proprietary technologies.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: Kurimoto is a leading player in Japan's infrastructure and industrial equipment sectors, competing with major domestic manufacturers of pipes, valves, and industrial machinery (such as Kubota, JFE Engineering, and Hitachi Zosen). The company differentiates itself through its integrated solutions and long-standing customer relationships.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: For the fiscal year ending March 2025, consolidated net sales were ¥126.7 billion, with operating profit of ¥7.9 billion and net profit attributable to shareholders of ¥6.9 billion, marking record-high profitability. The company has shown steady growth in sales and profits over recent years, with a strong balance sheet and a workforce of over 2,100 employees.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: Kurimoto emphasizes its ability to deliver comprehensive, customized solutions for social and industrial infrastructure, leveraging proprietary technologies, reliability, and a track record of trust with customers. Its focus on sustainability, safety, and lifecycle value, as well as its integrated manufacturing and engineering capabilities, set it apart in the market.
